page: Microsoft Azure L96as_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine built on AMD x86_64 processor architecture and managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features 96 dedicated vCPUs and 768.0 GB of memory, which establishes an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The hardware configuration does not feature graphical accelerators and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, focusing entirely on compute, memory density, and local storage throughput.

The server includes 23040 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage, providing substantial localized disk volume directly attached to the host node. This substantial NVMe footprint eliminates remote network hops for storage I/O, though operational designs must accommodate the ephemeral nature of direct-attached physical drives through external replication or managed backups.

From a cost-efficiency perspective relative to its hardware configuration, the integration of 23 TB of local NVMe SSDs reduces the reliance on independently provisioned high-IOPS network disks for intensive data operations. This architecture is well suited for storage-intensive and high-throughput transactional applications, including large distributed NoSQL datastores, relational databases, data warehousing platforms, and distributed search indexing systems.
description: Microsoft Azure L96as_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, powered by AMD x86_64 dedicated processors. It is configured with 96 dedicated vCPUs and 768.0 GB of RAM, offering an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The server integrates 23040 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage directly attached to the host, facilitating intensive I/O operations without relying solely on network-attached block devices. No graphics accelerators are included in this profile, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned. The server provides a high density of processing capacity, expansive memory, and extensive local flash storage within a single instance. This setup suits large-scale distributed NoSQL platforms, relational database management systems, big data analytics engines, data warehousing, and log search clusters that demand substantial localized disk space and high memory bandwidth.
